Question
========
What is the worst case actual useful size of a 4-way associative cache of 128 lines of 32 bytes?

Solution
========
The nominal capacity is 128 x 32 = 4096 bytes, spread over 128/4 = 32 rows.

In the worst case every address of the working set maps to the same row, so only the 4 ways of that single row are ever usable: 4 x 32 = 128 bytes.

This is the pathological case of a stride that is a multiple of the number of rows times the line size, and it is exactly why associativity exists at all.
